new_atom_sets.type_basis: A tool: its maker's blog and its paper's arXiv page, saved 2026-11-01, describe it as a feature in the Ai2 Playground that traces the outputs of language models back to their full training data in real time. Read on the site template.

evidence.record_quote: Today we introduce OLMoTrace, a one-of-a-kind feature in the Ai2 Playground that lets you trace the outputs of language models back to their full, multi-trillion-token training data in real time.
OLMoTrace finds and shows verbatim matches between segments of language model output and documents in the training text corpora.

atoms.reference: Ai2 (The Allen Institute for Artificial Intelligence), as a feature of the Ai2 Playground; the blog signed 'Jiacheng Liu et al.', the paper by Jiacheng Liu and 30 others.

evidence.record_quote: © The Allen Institute for Artificial Intelligence - All Rights Reserved.
by Jiacheng Liu and 30 other authors

atoms.reference: Introduced 9 April 2025 (the blog; arXiv v1 the same day); the paper in the ACL 2025 demo track.
Verbatim matches between segments of language model output and documents in the training text corpora: long and unique spans that appear verbatim at least once in the model's training data.

evidence.record_quote: OLMoTrace finds and shows verbatim matches between segments of language model output and documents in the training text corpora.
The highlights indicate long and unique spans that appear verbatim at least once in the training data of this model.

atoms.reference: The full training data of Ai2's three flagship models (OLMo 2 32B Instruct, OLMo 2 13B Instruct, OLMoE 1B 7B Instruct), for the 32B model five datasets of about 3.2 billion documents and 4.6 trillion tokens; applicable to any model whose training data is accessible.

evidence.record_quote: OLMoTrace is available today with our three flagship models: OLMo 2 32B Instruct , OLMo 2 13B Instruct , and OLMoE 1B 7B Instruct , and it can be applied to any language model for which you have access to the training data.
In total, these five datasets contain about 3.2 billion documents and 4.6 trillion tokens, and OLMoTrace matches against all of them.

atoms.reference: To enable researchers, developers and the general public to inspect where and how language models may have learned to generate certain word sequences; shown for fact checking, hallucination and creativity.

evidence.record_quote: We developed OLMoTrace to enable researchers, developers, and the general public to inspect where and how language models may have learned to generate certain word sequences.
We showcase how it can be used to explore fact checking, hallucination, and the creativity of language models.

atoms.reference: Publicly available and fully open-source, its source code released; the interpretation of matches called 'quite nuanced', and factual confidence left to the user's own verification of the documents' sources.

evidence.record_quote: OLMoTrace is publicly available and fully open-source.
We also release our source code .
The interpretation of text matches with training data is quite nuanced.
If you personally verify that these documents come from trusted sources, you can gain confidence that this piece of information generated by the model is factually correct.

atoms.reference: Built on infini-gram, with which the training data is indexed.

evidence.record_quote: To speed up computation, we index the training data with infini-gram and develop a novel parallel algorithm, reducing the time complexity of span finding from the naive O(L^2 * N) to O(L * log N)
